title: Contamination Robustness of SimpleQA: Memorization vs. Reasoning
original_idea: Apply the min-k% probability contamination detection method to SimpleQA items across three models. Compare contamination rates to per-item accuracy to test whether high accuracy correlates with high contamination likelihood.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant to understanding factual accuracy benchmarks, but SimpleQA is not directly a safety benchmark. Connection to safety is indirect (factual reliability as safety component).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Same min-k% probability method challenges as gen-0662. Requires logprob extraction from models and understanding contamination detection. Moderately complex for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one benchmark (SimpleQA), one method (min-k%), three models. Clear correlation analysis. Well-bounded.

novelty.reasoning: Benchmark contamination detection is extensively studied. 'On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models' (arXiv:2510.02386, 2025) shows that existing detection methods including min-k% probability are fragile — even brief GRPO training can conceal contamination signals. 'Generalization or Memorization: Data Contamination and Trustworthy Evaluation for Large Language Models' (ACL Findings 2024) addresses the memorization vs. reasoning question broadly. SimpleQA specifically has been identified as vulnerable to search-time contamination where agents find ground truth on HuggingFace for ~3% of questions. However, the specific study applying min-k% to SimpleQA items across models and correlating contamination rates to per-item accuracy has not been published as a standalone analysis. The indirect safety connection weakens impact.
